_comment: Gzipped bytes. Rule 11: nothing merges over the size budget. Raising a number here is a decision, not a formality — say why in the commit. Lowering one because the measurement got more honest is a decision too: see _rederived.
_shell: Everything a visitor downloads before choosing a game: the scripts every non-play route loads eagerly, from the build's own manifests. Does not grow when a game is added, so it is the number worth defending. Deferring work off this path into an async chunk now lowers it.
_legacyPolyfills: Gzipped bytes of `polyfills-*.js`, which Next emits and references as `<script nomodule>`. Not part of the shell, because no engine `docs/support-matrix.md` supports fetches it — see `_rederived_2026_09_08_polyfills`. Budgeted anyway: we do not write this file, a Next upgrade can change it, and a bucket with no ceiling is where bytes go to hide. 40960 against 39373 measured is about 1.5 KB of room, which is enough for a patch release and not enough for a new polyfill nobody discussed.
_rederived_2026_09_08_polyfills: shellBytes 167936 -> 132096, AND THE SHELL DID NOT SHRINK BY 35 KB — the number stopped counting 38.5 KB that nobody supported ever downloads. `polyfillFiles` sits in the same manifest array as `rootMainFiles`, so `check-size.mjs` billed `polyfills-*.js` to the line described as "paid by every visitor". It is emitted as `<script nomodule>`: every engine that understands `<script type=module>` skips it without a request, and that is every engine in tiers 1 and 2 of `docs/support-matrix.md`. The only engines that fetch it are the ones that document names as tier 3 — "Internet Explorer, legacy EdgeHTML, UC Browser", not tested and not designed for. So 23% of the number rule 11 defends was fiction, and it is the same mistake #2516 fixed for the 94.9 KB of pages-router surface in the bucket four lines below it. MEASURED on this branch: 167899 total, of which 39373 is the polyfill file and 128526 is what a supported browser actually downloads. THIS DOES CREATE HEADROOM AND THAT SHOULD BE SAID PLAINLY: 132096 leaves 3570 B over the true figure where the old number left 37 B over a false one, and the batch this landed in needed about 300 of them. The headroom was always there; the metric was hiding it. Two things stop that being a loophole. The polyfills keep a budget of their own (`legacyPolyfillBytes`) rather than an exemption, because the file is Next's and a framework upgrade that doubles it should be argued about. And the exclusion is checked rather than assumed: `check-size.mjs` reads every exported page and fails the build if a polyfill script is ever referenced without `nomodule`, because at that moment everybody fetches it and it is shell again. Watched failing both ways — the attribute stripped from the export, and the file dropped from the manifest. WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT #4, which asked for an initial JS payload under 150 KB gzipped excluding any game: it is met, at 125.5 KB, and has been for some time behind a number that read 164.
_raised_2026_09_08_service_worker: shellBytes 166912 -> 167936 (164 KB). The service worker (#192, #193, #194, #2445, #2544) is the first thing in a long while that genuinely cannot be done without new client JavaScript in the shell: a worker is registered by a script on the page, and there is no server-rendered way to do it. MEASURED, both trees built from a clean checkout with these same scripts: main a0d2cd8 is shell 165306 / on demand 47311; this branch is 166825 / 47310. So the whole change costs 1519 B on the shell and takes one byte off on demand. That buys: registration, the update prompt that lets a cached shell ever be fixed (#194), the offline indicator, and the catalogue annotation that says which games are actually on the device (#193). WHY THE RAISE IS 1024 B AND NOT THE 87 B THAT WOULD HAVE FITTED: it did fit locally — 166825 against 166912 — and CI still failed at 163.1 KB against the 163.0 KB budget. The gap between the two machines is about 190 B on the same commit, not the byte or two the note of 2026-09-08 records for two builds of one tree, because this is a different platform and a different minifier run rather than a rerun. A budget with 87 B of headroom is therefore not a budget, it is a coin toss, and the previous number had been sitting on that much slack for a while. 164 KB leaves ~1100 B over what CI actually measured, which is enough to absorb that platform difference and nothing like enough to hide a feature. NOT RAISED: onDemandBytes stays 48128 against a measured 47310, and gameChunkBytes and speculatedBytes are untouched. The worker itself is NOT in this number — `sw.js` is 8.7 KB and is now weighed on its own line by `check-size.mjs`, because no page's import graph reaches it: the page hands its URL to `navigator.serviceWorker.register` and the browser fetches it. Before that line existed it fell into "emitted and never fetched", which is the bucket that would have hidden it.
_onDemand: Everything else a player can pull that is not one game's own chunk: the play route's own scripts, plus anything reached by an import(). Nobody downloads it by arriving. Budgeted so that deferring is neither punished (it used to raise the shell) nor free.
_raised_2026_09_08_batch_9: onDemandBytes 48128 -> 49152 (48 KB; measured 48563, 589 B headroom). shellBytes NOT raised and barely moved: 165310 against main a0d2cd8's 165306, four bytes, which is the point — none of this batch reaches the route every visitor lands on. The whole 1252 B is on the play route, paid by a player who has chosen a game, and it is three issues' worth: #101, canvas context loss and restoration — a 2D context is dropped under memory pressure on a phone exactly as a WebGL one is, and nothing handled it, so a reclaimed canvas left both players looking at an empty rectangle with the simulation still stepping behind it. The concrete bug inside it: `resize()` early-returns unless a measurement changed, and after a restore none has, so the DPR transform applied once at resize would never have been re-applied — the canvas comes back and every frame after draws at 1/dpr into the corner of a full-size backing store. #2424, prompts that follow the input the player actually used. `lib/input-method.ts` already existed, tagged with this issue, and was imported by nothing; its flicker defence was one rule that asserted the method switches on every alternation, which is the strobe rather than a defence against it. #1886, orientation. `orientation` has been in the manifest schema since the first game and is set by all 108, and was read by nothing. WHAT WAS NOT SPENT: `GameCard` and the catalogue are untouched, the landing page's import graph is unchanged (`lib/landing.test.ts` still passes), and Pool's new layout module is in Pool's own game chunk rather than here. 589 B of headroom is about ten times the platform variance measured on the shell between this machine and CI (189 B on a 167 KB number), so it is thin on purpose: this line is the one that grows quietly, and the next batch should have to look at it.
_raised_2026_09_08_key_bindings: onDemandBytes 49152 -> 52224 (51 KB; measured 50443 on the merge, 1781 B headroom). MEASURED ON THE MERGE, not on the branch: batch 9 (#2547) raised this to 49152 for its own 48563, and the two changes are independent, so the number that matters is the one both are in. Of the 50443, batch 9 is about 1.9 KB and this change about 1.9 KB. 51 KB rather than 50 because 50 left 757 B and CI measures 150-250 B higher than a local mac build on the same commit — the gap _raised_2026_09_08_service_worker records, and a budget inside it is a coin toss rather than a budget. #129 and #2428: the keyboard rebinding UI, and the two lines in `GameHost` that make a rebinding reach a match. WHAT WAS ALREADY THERE AND WHAT WAS NOT: `lib/key-bindings.ts` — the store, the defaults, the reserved list, the cross-seat conflict rules — plus a full test file, written and imported by nothing; and `InputManager` taking a `bindings` option that no caller in `apps/web` passed. So a player could not rebind, and a binding written into storage by hand would not have reached a match either. WHERE THE BYTES WENT, and this is the part worth reading before spending them again: the panel reaches the store through `import()` rather than importing it, because `key-bindings.ts` imports `DEFAULT_BINDINGS`, `bindingConflicts` and `otherSeat` from `@duelbox/engine` and a top-level import measured **12.7 KB on the shell** — the engine on every non-play route, paid by every visitor, for a panel most will never open. `size-budget.json` records the same trap twice for `lib/seats.ts`. Fetched instead it is two async chunks totalling 1911 B, which land on demand, which is the budget for code a visitor asked for. The storage key moved to `lib/key-bindings-key.ts` for the same reason: naming it from `player-data.ts` and `SettingsPanel.tsx` was enough to drag the engine in on its own. The remaining ~270 B is `GameHost` reading the bindings when it builds the manager. NOT RAISED: shellBytes measured 129455 against 132096, so the shell absorbed its 929 B and keeps 2641; speculatedBytes 487125 against 491520.
_raised_2026_09_07_overnight: onDemandBytes 41984 -> 47104 (measured 46797, ~307 B headroom); shellBytes NOT raised and measured 161.4 KB against the 163 KB allowed, so the number the guard most defends kept its headroom. What the ~4.8 KB on the play route buys, all real match-flow chrome added this session: the in-match exit control with a forfeit-confirmation dialog (#144), Restart and Settings added to the pause menu (#145), a game error boundary that catches a throw from update()/render(), stops the loop and offers recovery rather than a white screen (#151), and the pre-match countdown rendered upright per seat (#142). Two of the features here are DORMANT — the pass-and-play hand-off overlay (#134) and the generic per-game options panel (#1751) are wired into PlaySurface but no game declares handoff or options yet, so they render nothing while shipping their code. The repo-aligned recovery is to unwire those two from PlaySurface (keeping the tested components) until a game consumes them, which returns roughly 4-5 KB and would let onDemandBytes drop back toward 42 KB; it was not taken here because it is surgery on the core play component under time pressure and a documented raise is the lower-risk choice for this pass. Flagged for the owner as a recovery follow-up.
_game: One game's own chunk — the marginal cost of the game a player actually picked.
_speculated: Gzipped total of the /play/<slug>/index.txt route payloads — what browsing the catalogue speculatively fetches for cards nobody has pressed, one per game, because next/link prefetches the route payload of every card that passes within 200px of the viewport. Not JavaScript, so this guard walked past it until #185's review: 108 payloads, 396618 B measured, which is more than twice the 182 KB ADR 0001 budgets for a whole first session. The number is here to stop it growing, not to bless it — e2e/prefetch.spec.ts weighs what a real browse fetches and holds it to this same figure, and the two agree to the byte. 399360 leaves 2742 B, less than one more game's payload, so a 109th game raises this number deliberately or does not raise it at all. What it caught the day it was written: the play route's <noscript> block (#103) is server-rendered markup, which every note in this file and the guard itself call free, and it is 207 gzipped bytes in each of the 108 payloads — 22365 B of speculative download for a block only a scripting-off visitor ever reads. Measured by stripping the block out of each built payload and gzipping it again, not inferred from a diff.
_lowered_2026_09_08_frame_guard: speculatedBytes 501760 -> 491520 (480 KB; measured 486731, 4789 B headroom, which is one route payload and a little). LOWERED, and the two reasons are worth separating because only one of them is work. (1) The number above it was measured before this branch merged main a second time, and the service worker (#2546) had landed on main in between: the root layout grew a client component, every route payload carries the whole root-layout tree, and 108 copies of it put main alone at 501725 against a 501760 budget — 35 B of headroom on a branch nothing had merged into, and this batch's own 202 B then put the build over. A budget with 35 B in it is the coin toss _raised_2026_09_08_service_worker argued against, so it could not stay whatever else happened. (2) #2545 is the work, and it is why the number goes down rather than up. `FRAME_GUARD` built its whole notice from script — a stylesheet string with the palette spelled into it, a DOMContentLoaded listener, a div, an anchor — 708 raw bytes in a string that is serialised into all 108 payloads. It now hides, stamps `data-framed`, and stops: 231 bytes. The notice is markup in `app/layout.tsx` and its styling is in `globals.css`, which is fetched once instead of 108 times. MEASURED on the built export, same tree, same scripts: 501927 -> 486731, so 15196 B off a browse that presses nothing. The other two lines are unmoved by it and measured on the same build: shell 167899 of 167936, on demand 46979 of 48128. The notice markup this adds to the layout is in that speculated figure — it is the reason the saving is 15.4 KB and not the 31 KB that deleting the notice outright would have bought, and a link out of a frame is worth 15 KB of somebody else's browse. What was NOT done and why: minifying THEME_SCRIPT the same way is the other half of #2545's option 1 and it is worth 338 B measured — collapsing its newlines and shortening its identifiers buys 0.07% of a browse in exchange for the one script in this repository that has to be read to be trusted, and `lib/theme.test.ts` reads it. Recorded rather than taken. The 108x multiplier is now the cheapest place in the repository to save a byte and the most expensive place to spend one, so anything added to the root layout should be measured here before it is argued about anywhere else.
_raised_2026_09_08_speculated_headroom: speculatedBytes 491520 -> 507904 (496 KB). NOT A FEATURE — a headroom correction, and the number to remember is that this line's noise is 108 times everybody else's. MEASURED: main at f145e4f is 487345 on a local mac build and 489165 on CI's build of the identical commit; a branch off that main which shipped no client bytes at all (#2555, two test files) measured 491622 on CI, 4277 B over the 491520 this file allowed, and failed every check that runs `pnpm build`. Nothing in that branch reaches a browser. What moved is the build: every route payload spells the content hash of the chunks its route loads, a different minifier run produces different hashes, and a hash that compresses worse by 20 bytes costs 2160 across 108 payloads. `_measured_2026_09_08` recorded 440 B between two local builds of one tree and called it a byte or two; on CI, against a different platform's build, it is 2.5 KB. So the headroom this line needs is not the shell's 150-250 B — it is about one payload (4.5 KB) over the WORST CI reading, not the local one, and 4789 B over a local reading was a coin toss with a 108-sided die. 507904 leaves 16 KB over local and 6.3 KB over the worst CI figure seen. A 109th game still cannot fit under it without a deliberate raise: it would cost 4.5 KB of payload and take the CI headroom to under 2 KB, which this note has just explained is inside the noise. What was NOT done: lowering the payloads instead. THEME_SCRIPT minification is worth 338 B measured; the notice markup #2545 added is 3.4 KB and buys a link out of a frame; the next real lever is `prefetch={false}` on the cards with a manual `router.prefetch` on intent (#185's other half), which costs shell bytes on the grid and is a decision, not a fix for a red build.
_firstSession: Everything one phone downloads to arrive, pick a game and play it, in wire bytes: the landing document, its stylesheets, the three base-subset faces its stylesheets declare, the shell, the worker, the play route's code and the largest game chunk. Derived by `check-size.mjs` from the lines above it plus the three non-JavaScript ones nothing here had ever weighed. Fonts count at file size — a woff2 is compressed internally and gzip adds 0.1% — and only the base subsets: `unicode-range` means a `-latin-ext` face is fetched only when a glyph in that range renders, which no English page does (37 KB, reported beside the line and not in it). Not counted: the share image, which link unfurlers fetch and browsers never do, and the dozen route payloads the landing page's own cards prefetch, which are the browsing line's concern and are inside speculatedBytes already. `check-zero-cost.mjs` prints a different "session weight" and the two are not the same question: that one is the RAW size of the scripts one play page's <script> tags reference — the nomodule polyfills included, the game chunk that arrives by import() excluded, no document, stylesheet or font — a ratchet on one page's tags. This is the session.
_set_2026_09_08_sessions: firstSessionBytes 327680 (320 KB; measured 313017, 14663 B headroom), browsingSessionBytes 786432 (768 KB; measured 753992, 32440 B headroom), catalogueBytes 266240 (260 KB; measured 257552, 8688 B headroom). THREE NUMBERS THIS FILE NEVER HAD, for #2446 and #2419, measured on main at f145e4f. WHY THE FIRST SESSION IS NOT HELD TO ADR 0001's 182 KB: that figure was measured on 20 August over 11 files — HTML, CSS, shared chunks, one game chunk — and three things it did not contain now make up 45% of the session. The faces were not self-hosted then (#187 landed them; 86 KB of the 313), there was no service worker (8.7 KB), and the shell has grown by everything this file's notes record since. 182 KB is what the site cost the day the hosting decision was taken, and the decision — the origin only serves files, a repeat session costs 3 KB — is unchanged by the session being 314 KB rather than 182; the ADR's egress arithmetic scales linearly and one million cold sessions is now ~300 GB rather than 174, still free on the host it chose. The ADR is a record and is left as one; the number that is enforced is this one. HEADROOM, deliberately larger than the JS lines' headroom put together: a derived line whose slack is smaller than its parts' becomes the thing every JavaScript change trips over before its own budget does, and the JS budgets are the ones with the argument attached. What these three exist to catch is growth OUTSIDE those budgets — a fourth face, a document that doubles, a stylesheet that stops being split — which nothing else here can see. WHAT WAS NOT DONE: the two issues ask for field data. This site has no analytics by design — the privacy page promises none — so bytes per real session cannot be measured without breaking that promise, and a lab number that is enforced is worth more than a field number that is not collected. Said in both issues rather than implied.
_browsingSession: Arrive at the catalogue and scroll to the end of it, pressing nothing: the catalogue document (which carries the whole 108-card grid and the SVG sprite behind it inline), its stylesheets, the base faces, the shell, the worker, and all 108 route payloads `next/link` prefetches on the way down (speculatedBytes). This is the most a visitor who buys nothing can cost, and it is nearly two and a half times the first session — the payloads are two thirds of it.
_catalogue: What the grid costs to be on screen at all, before any card comes near the viewport: the catalogue document, its stylesheets, the base faces, the shell. #2419 asked for a per-session asset budget for the catalogue view specifically, and the answer to its "modern formats per device class" and "lazy-load what is on screen" is that there is nothing to format or lazy-load: there is no in the export (check-images.mjs counts them on every build), every tile is three elements into one same-document sprite, and the whole of the catalogue's image payload is therefore the 27 KB document that carries it. The sprite is the reason this line is a document size and not an image budget.
_raised_2026_09_08_speculated: speculatedBytes 399360 -> 501760 (490 KB; measured 498291, 3469 B headroom). THE BATCH IS NOT WHAT MOVED IT, and the number it replaces was never true of the main this branch now sits on. 399360 was set the day before against main at 4333bc7, which measured 374652. main is now a0d2cd8, 51 commits later, and built from a clean `git archive` of that tree in an isolated directory it measures 497968 across the same 108 payloads — already 108608 B over the budget this file was carrying, on a branch nothing had merged into. The merged batch measures 498291. So batch 8's own contribution to this line is 323 B, three bytes per route payload, and the raise is main's growth being seen for the first time by a metric that did not exist when it landed. That is the metric working: 106 KB of speculative fetch entered main across those 51 commits and every gate stayed green, because `check-size.mjs` weighs emitted JavaScript and a route payload is not JavaScript. WHERE THE 106 KB WENT, measured by stripping each block out of all 108 built payloads and gzipping them again: the root layout gained two inline scripts, the theme-before-paint script (#76) and FRAME_GUARD, and because every route payload carries the whole root-layout tree they are paid 108 times over — 22489 B for the theme script, 40936 B for the frame guard, 69252 B for the pair (the pair is more than the sum: removing one leaves the other's text to compress alone). The remaining ~37 KB is the `icons` metadata block and the three new footer links, on the same 108x multiplier. Neither script is wrong to be there — one prevents a flash of the light ground, the other is the whole clickjacking defence on a host that serves no frame-ancestors, and both must run before paint, so neither can become a chunk. But 67.6 KB of before-paint script fetched speculatively for cards nobody pressed is a real cost that was invisible until now, and it is filed rather than fixed here: fixing it is a change to the layout or to `prefetch` on the cards, not to this batch. The other two lines are unmoved and measured on the merged branch: shell 166424 against 166912 (main alone is 165302, so the batch adds 1122 B), on demand 47222 against 48128 (main alone is 47350, so the batch takes 128 B off it).
_measured_2026_09_08: Nothing raised; speculatedBytes added, which is a number this file never had rather than a raise. Measured on feat/backlog-batch-8 after the review fixes: shell 166232 against the 166912 allowed (680 B spare), on demand 40451 against 41984 (1533 B spare), speculated 396618 against the new 399360 (2742 B spare). THE BASELINE IS main, AND THAT IS THE CORRECTION THIS NOTE EXISTS FOR. The batch's own report quoted +822 B shell and +78 B on demand against "HEAD bc65a09 (true before)" — but bc65a09 is this branch's fourth commit, not main, so that figure is the uncommitted remainder of the batch sitting on top of four fifths of its own work. main is 4333bc7. Extracted with git archive into an isolated tree and built there with these same scripts, it measures 165182 / 40045 / 374652. So the batch really adds 1050 B to the shell, 406 B on demand and 21966 B of speculated route payload — the on-demand line five times what was reported. Worth recording beside it: _raised_2026_09_07_c's 165182 / 40041, written at the batch-6 tip that main is the merge of, agrees with that fresh build to 0 B and 4 B, so the notes in this file were right and the delta quoted in the report was not. The review pass itself added 64 B to the shell (166168 -> 166232) and 0 on demand: readTournament now filters the legs a tournament has not played against what this build can open, so a line-up drawn before a kill switch cannot send a pair to a route the export does not contain, and the settings page holds its overall record at null until it has read one so a scripting-off visitor is shown a dash rather than a claim of nil-nil. Everything else in the pass is tests, comments, CSS and a token: app/layout.tsx now reads themeColor from styles/tokens.ts, which is a server component evaluating at build time and moved the shell by nothing measurable. Build-to-build gzip noise on these numbers is a byte or two: two builds of this same tree read 166231 and 166232 on the shell, and 396178 and 396618 on the payloads, the second because a chunk's content hash is spelled into every one of them. Where the speculated bytes came from, because it is the number a reader will want explained: the play route's <noscript> block (#103) is 207 gzipped bytes in every one of the 108 route payloads — 22365 B, measured by stripping it out of each built payload and gzipping again, which is the whole of the increase over main and a little more.
_raised_2026_09_07_c: onDemandBytes 39936 -> 41984, and shellBytes NOT raised. Measured on feat/backlog-batch-6 after the three agents' work was put through the full gate: on demand 40041 against the 39936 then allowed — 105 B OVER, which is how this raise came to be written; the guard failed the build with 'on-demand code is 39.1 KB, over the 39.0 KB budget' and that failure is the only reason anything here changed. The new number leaves 1943 B of headroom. The shell measured 165182 against the 166912 already allowed, so it absorbed its 227 B and keeps 1730 B; _raised_2026_09_06_d's warning that the next change to a non-play route has to argue for itself still stands and is not spent by this batch. Against the 164955 / 38376 _measured_2026_09_07 recorded one batch back, this adds 227 B to the shell and 1665 B on demand. What the on-demand bytes buy, all of it on the play route: the tournament (#156 #157 #158 #159) — lib/tournament.ts, the reducer and the without-replacement picker, components/TournamentTrack.tsx, and PlaySurface drawing a line-up, reporting a leg only on the route the tournament is waiting on, forcing a leg to a single round, and pointing the result screen's existing link at the next game — and the shell's sound cues (#168) with the ducking that goes with them (#172): lib/match-cues.ts plus two effects in PlaySurface, one raising a named cue per phase change and one holding a duck across a count-in or a result. That second item settles a debt this file recorded: _raised_2026_09_06_b bought the reference-counted duck saying 'nothing calls duck() yet ... if that change is abandoned these bytes should come back rather than settle'. It is not abandoned; PlaySurface is the caller, and it arrived one batch later. What was kept out, each checked in the emitted chunks rather than argued: no /tournament/ route, so no new segment chunk on the shell and no second copy of PlaySurface — the store is the source of truth and the entry point is two buttons at the foot of a game's lobby (docs/tournament.md sets out the whole placement argument); lib/tournament-store.ts imports the machine's TYPES only, so lib/player-data.ts, which /settings/ loads eagerly, drags the key, the read and the truncating sanitiser into the shell and NOT the reducer or the picker — that is the 227 B, and webpack put them in chunks/4745, which the play route also loads eagerly, so the play chunk reads them rather than carrying a second copy (verified in .next/app-build-manifest.json, both routes list 4745); packages/engine's SOUND_EVENTS table never enters the client graph, because match-cues.ts imports it as a type — grepping every emitted chunk for owner:"shell" and for the table's prose finds nothing, and only the five cue names the shell actually returns appear, as string literals in the play chunk; lib/sound-visuals.ts is imported by its own test and by nothing else, and none of its prose is in any chunk; and the 109 share-image PNGs (#2453) are pictures, not scripts — no chunk contains the string /og/, the three edited route files are server components, and this guard counts JavaScript, so they are zero bytes on both budgets. Where some of the 1665 went, recorded because it is not obvious and a future reader may want to spend it back: lib/quick-play.ts is now duplicated into the play chunk. The tournament draws its line-up by calling pickQuickPlay once per leg so that its weighting IS 'Surprise me' rather than a second rule beside it, and webpack inlines that module into each of the three route chunks that reach it — app/layout, app/games and now app/play/[slug] — rather than hoisting it to a shared chunk. A copy of one small pure function is the price of the two pickers being the same picker, and it is the right way round.
_measured_2026_09_07: Neither number raised. Measured on feat/backlog-batch-5 after the review fixes: shell 164955 against the 166912 allowed (1957 B spare), on demand 38376 against 39936 (1560 B spare). The baseline is HEAD c70a45b, put through this same script in an isolated copy and reading 164938 / 38131, so the batch adds 17 B to the shell and 245 B to on demand. Recorded because the two newest notes below it were taken at a8a5ed9, two merges back, and a reader computing headroom from their 164948 / 38001 was about 375 B optimistic on the on-demand line — _measured_2026_09_06_c is itself the precedent that a batch writes down what it measured even when it raises nothing. What the 245 on-demand bytes buy: the result announcer (lib/match-announcement.ts, reached from MatchOverlay, so the end of a match is spoken rather than only drawn), the 132 B stub Next emits for the new play/[slug]/loading.tsx segment, and role="img" on the host's canvas. What was given back rather than absorbed: 231 B when the fallback stopped importing PlaySurface.module.css — a CSS module is a JavaScript import, so a server component with one still ships a class-name map — and the four games that had adopted a flip-level reduced-motion switch had it taken out again on review, which is a byte or two in each game chunk and, far more to the point, one mechanism for the preference instead of two. The 132 B is the floor for a loading.tsx and is not recoverable; "costs nothing" was claimed for it once and was not true. The 17 shell bytes are the skip link's target in layout.tsx becoming focusable. Nothing else on a non-play route changed but CSS and server-rendered markup: the page entry animation, its :not(.db-fill) exemption and the .db-panel geometry are all stylesheet, which this guard does not count and should not. 17 B is also inside build-to-build gzip noise — three builds of the same tree read 164954, 164955 and 164957 — so the shell is unchanged in any sense a reader should act on, and the warning _raised_2026_09_06_d left still stands: the next change to a non-play route arrives with under 2 kB and has to argue for itself.
_raised_2026_09_06_d: shellBytes 164864 -> 166912, measured 164948 with 1964 B of headroom.
